notes: FGBFM 40 (Scott & Burgan 2005) is deliberately not used: it is calibrated on US fuels and has no Papuan analogue.
The map is a reclassification of three global products, not a classification. There is no fuel ground truth for Biak, so no accuracy or validation is claimed.

Dynamic World is reduced to its per-pixel mode over a window that ends before the first August 2026 detection, because the product reads burned ground as bare. Land pixels with no Dynamic World scene in the window are counted separately and excluded from the 6x6 matrix.
TMF is 30 m and is upsampled to the 10 m output grid with nearest neighbour. The closed-forest/regrowth split is therefore blocky at 30 m; the WorldCover and Dynamic World classes keep 10 m detail.
WorldCover class 90 (herbaceous wetland) is mapped to nonfuel. It can carry burning when dry, and its area is reported separately so the choice can be re-cut.

TMF class 2 (degraded) is mapped to closed forest as the conservative choice; its area is reported separately. Tree cover that TMF does not resolve also stays closed forest and is reported separately.
Hotspots are where satellites saw heat, not a random sample of land. A class over-represented among them is an association, not a cause, and no significance test is computed.
The class names describe expected burning behaviour. They are not fuel load, moisture, rate of spread, flame length, or inputs to a spread model.

The free-text notes are one interpreter's incidental remarks, written for a different question. The fuel class at each noted box is printed as a spot-check only; no agreement figure is computed from it.
